editorial.headline: Household Goods Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retailing brooms, brushes, mats and mopping articles can be fully foreign-owned nationally, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**Nationally, this is an entirely foreign-open retail activity. In Bali today, however, a foreigner cannot register it through PMA.** The national ceiling is 100%, but the Bali outcome is a block, not a reduced ownership allowance. Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium prevents PMA registration for activities carrying Low or Medium-Low risk. For this activity, OSS places the Large scale at Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope, bringing it within the block recorded from May 13, 2026. Nationally open to full foreign ownership does not make this activity registrable for PMA in Bali.

The activity itself is retail trade in other household equipment and supplies not classified elsewhere within its household-goods subdivision. The record gives a practical view of the merchandise: twig brooms, fibre brooms, brushes, mats, mops and mop cloths. These examples define a retail category centred on household cleaning and related supplies. Its scope is deliberately residual: it covers the household articles within the subdivision that are not otherwise classified there, rather than being confined to one named product.

The registration field is broad in scale. The record marks the activity open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses. Across those stated scales, the commercial activity remains the same described retail trade: household equipment and supplies of the kind represented by brooms, brushes, mats and mopping articles. The scale listing does not change the nature of the category; it identifies the business sizes to which the record opens it.

The national and Bali positions must therefore be read separately. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA and maximum foreign ownership is 100%, making full foreign ownership available under the cited Presidential Regulations. In Bali, the decisive point is the recorded risk-class block at the Large scale. The moratorium is island-wide and permanent, and the record says it blocks PMA registration in Bali for this activity. For a foreign founder considering Bali, the conclusion is plain: this activity may be nationally open, yet it cannot be registered there through PMA today.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to full foreign ownership does not make this activity registrable for PMA in Bali.
